notes.title: Chuseok
notes.text: 추석 (also called 한가위) is the autumn harvest festival, on the 15th day of the 8th lunar month. Families travel home, hold 차례 (a memorial rite for ancestors) in the morning, visit family graves, and eat 송편 — half-moon rice cakes filled with sesame, beans or chestnuts.

scene.ko: 추석 첫날 아침. 할머니의 막내 딸이 미국에서 귀국했어요.
scene.en: The first morning of Chuseok. Grandma's youngest daughter has flown home from America.

scene.ko: 엄마! 보고 싶었어요!
scene.en: Mom! I missed you!

scene.ko: 아이고, 우리 딸! 미국에서 교포로 산 지 십 년이야. 귀국은 오 년 만이지?
scene.en: Oh, my girl! Ten years living in America. And this is your first time home in five years, isn't it?

scene.ko: 네. 이번에는 열흘 동안 있을 거예요. 사흘은 서울, 닷새는 강릉, 이틀은 부산.
scene.en: Yes. This time I'm staying ten days. Three in Seoul, five in Gangneung, two in Busan.

scene.ko: 처음 뵙겠습니다. 저는 제이미예요.

notes.title: Counting days
notes.text: Korean has native words for spans of days: 하루 (1 day), 이틀 (2), 사흘 (3), 나흘 (4), 닷새 (5), 열흘 (10). Also: 엊그제 (a couple of days ago), 모레 (the day after tomorrow), 이튿날 (the next day). At holidays, younger family members give elders a deep bow (큰절) with wishes like 건강하세요.

notes.title: -게 하다
notes.text: -게 하다 means "make or let someone do": 지우를 가져오게 해 (have Ji-woo bring it), 사람을 웃게 해요 (it makes people laugh). On national holidays like 개천절 (October 3, Korea's founding day), many families hang the 태극기 (the national flag) by the front door.

lessons.goal: Compare the past and the present.

notes.title: Talking about time
notes.text: 옛날 / 예전 / 과거 = the old days, the past; 오늘날 / 현대 = today, modern times; 요새 / 최근 = these days, recently. 원래 and 본래 both mean "originally." 옛 and 오랜 only go before nouns: 옛 친구 (an old friend), 오랜 전통 (a long tradition).

notes.title: The Chuseok moon
notes.text: On Chuseok night, families step outside to see the year's brightest full moon (보름달) and make a wish (소원을 빌다). Time words: 이날 (that day), 밤중 (the middle of the night), 한동안 (for a while), 오랫동안 (for a long time), 평생 (one's whole life).

lessons.goal: Talk about years: last year, this year, every year.

scene.ko: 엄마, 내일 미국에 돌아가요. 이번 추석은 금년 최고의 시간이었어요.

scene.en: From now on I'll come every year. Every single Chuseok! I promise.

notes.title: Year words
notes.text: 올해 / 금년 (this year — 금년 is formal), 작년 / 지난해 (last year), 재작년 (the year before last), 내년 (next year), 매년 / 해마다 (every year), 연말 (the end of the year), 새해 (the New Year). The New Year greeting: 새해 복 많이 받으세요!
